bands.1:
Three badges! The crew is having a party on the Soggy Biscuit.

Mo has made a sardine trifle. Nobody eats it. On the radio, the Reef Rays are losing, as usual.

Then Maxx goes live. He is on a gold couch. He looks sad.

"Vantafam, this is a family special," he sniffs. "My little sister ran away. Wrennie, if you are watching, please come home."

He holds up a photo of a small girl holding a sick possum.

Everyone on the boat goes quiet. It is Wren.

"Smash that heart button for Wrennie!" says Maxx.

Wren turns off the tablet. Her hands are shaking.

"My name is Wren Bottomley," she says. "His real name is Max Bottomley. He changed it."

Mo snorts. "Bottomley?"

"He thought Vantablack sounded cooler," says Wren.

She tells you everything. When they were little, they saved that possum together. Max was kind back then. Then his channel got big. He needed bigger rescues. One day, Wren found a room full of cages on his yacht. So she took his map and ran.

"I didn't tell you," she says. "I thought you'd think I was a spy."

"Plot twist!" says Zed. "I did not see that coming."

"Does he have gold bogeys?" asks Gus.

Indi hands Wren a drawing. It shows the whole crew. Wren is in the middle.

Then everyone looks at you.

"She stays," you say. "She's crew."

Wren smiles for the first time all day. Mo hands her the trifle. She eats a whole spoonful.

Then someone knocks on the side of the boat. Knock, knock, knock.

A girl in a purple jacket climbs on board.

"Hi," she says. "I'm Kaydence Kray. I know who you are. I know who she is. And I want to help you take Maxx down."

"I'll film from my speedboat," she adds. "Heists are terrible for my hair."

Her camera is already filming.
bands.2:
Three badges! The crew is having a party on the deck of the Soggy Biscuit.

Mo has made a victory trifle with layers of custard, jelly and sardines. Nobody touches it. Tully has the footy on the radio, and the Reef Rays are losing by forty points, as usual.

Then the tablet buzzes. Maxx is live.

This time, Maxx isn't smiling. He's sitting on a gold couch, dabbing his eyes with a gold tissue.

"Vantafam, this is a family special," he sniffs. "My little sister ran away from home. Wrennie, if you're watching, please come back. I miss you."

He holds up a photo. It shows a small girl with a missing front tooth, holding a sick possum wrapped in a towel.

Everyone on the boat goes silent. It's Wren.

"Smash that heart button for Wrennie!" sobs Maxx.

Wren switches off the tablet. Her hands are shaking.

"My name is Wren Bottomley," she says quietly. "And his real name is Max Bottomley. He changed it."

Mo snorts so hard that custard comes out of his nose. "Bottomley?"

"He thought Vantablack sounded cooler," says Wren.

Then she tells you everything. When they were little, they nursed that possum back to health together. Max was kind back then. But when his channel got big, he needed bigger and bigger rescues. One day, Wren found a room full of cages on his yacht. That night, she took his map and ran.

"I didn't tell you because I thought you'd think I was a spy," she says.

"Plot twist!" says Zed. "I did not see that cutscene coming."

"Statistically," says Tully, "one in ten crews has a secret sibling."

"That's not a real statistic," says Indi.

"It is now."

"Does he have gold bogeys?" asks Gus.

"Gus!" says Indi. She tears a page out of her sketchbook and hands it to Wren. It's a drawing of the whole crew, with Wren in the middle.

Then everyone looks at you.

"She stays," you say. "She's crew."

Wren smiles for the first time all day. Mo hands her the trifle, and she eats a whole spoonful without complaining. That is true friendship.

Then someone knocks on the side of the boat. Knock, knock, knock.

A girl in a purple jacket climbs aboard, with a ring light glowing on her helmet.

"Hi," she says. "I'm Kaydence Kray, the second-biggest streamer in the world. I know who you are. I know who she is. And I want to help you take Maxx down."

"I'll film from my speedboat, the Clickbait," she adds. "Heists are terrible for my hair."

Her camera is already filming.

bands.4:
Three badges! The crew is having a party on the deck of the Soggy Biscuit, and Zed has strung a tangle of fairy lights along the mast, only half of which work.

Mo has made a victory trifle with layers of custard, lime jelly and sardines. It quivers ominously whenever anyone walks past, and once, nobody is quite sure, it seems to burp. Nobody touches it. Tully has the footy on the radio, and the Reef Rays are losing by forty points, as usual.

Then the tablet buzzes. Maxx is live.

This time, Maxx isn't smiling. He's sitting on a gold velvet couch in a dimly lit room, dabbing at his eyes with a gold tissue. Sad piano music tinkles in the background, and a single gold candle flickers beside him.

"Vantafam, this is a family special," he sniffs. "My little sister ran away from home. Wrennie, if you're watching, please come back. I miss you so, so much."

He holds up a faded photo. It shows a small girl with a missing front tooth, cradling a sick possum wrapped in a striped beach towel.

Everyone on the boat goes completely silent, except the trifle, which wobbles. It's Wren.

"Smash that heart button for Wrennie!" sobs Maxx, as the hearts pour in.

Wren reaches out and switches off the tablet. Her hands are shaking.

"My name is Wren Bottomley," she says quietly. "And his real name is Max Bottomley. He changed it when he got famous."

Mo snorts so violently that custard shoots out of his nose. "Bottomley?"

"He thought Vantablack sounded cooler," says Wren, and for a second she almost laughs.

Then she tells you everything. When they were little, they found that possum by the side of the road and nursed it back to health in a shoebox under Max's bed. Max was kind back then, and funny, and he loved animals just as much as she did. But when his channel took off, he needed bigger and bigger rescues to keep the Vantafam watching, and the Creatures he rescued began to look more frightened every week. One night, Wren found a room full of cages hidden below the deck of his yacht. Before sunrise, she had taken his map and run.

"I didn't tell you because I thought you'd think I was a spy," she says, staring at the deck. "Or worse, that I was just like him."

"Plot twist!" says Zed, eyes wide. "I genuinely did not see that cutscene coming."

"Statistically," says Tully, "one in ten crews has a secret sibling."

"That's not a real statistic," says Indi.

"It is now."

"Does he have gold bogeys?" asks Gus, who seems genuinely curious.

"Gus!" says Indi. Then she tears a page out of her sketchbook and hands it to Wren. It's a drawing of the whole crew squashed onto the deck of the Soggy Biscuit, with Wren right in the middle, holding a possum.

Then, slowly, everyone turns to look at you.

You think about all the things Wren knew that she shouldn't have, and all the times she said "lucky guess" and looked away. You think about the Creatures she has carried out of cages with her own hands.

"She stays," you say. "She's crew."

Wren smiles for the first time all day, a wobbly smile that turns into a real one. Mo hands her the trifle, and she eats a whole spoonful without complaining. Everyone agrees that this is true friendship.

Then someone knocks on the side of the boat. Knock, knock, knock.

A girl in a glossy purple jacket climbs aboard, a ring light glowing on her helmet like a halo.

"Hi," she says, flashing a smile that is almost as bright as Maxx's. "I'm Kaydence Kray, the second-biggest streamer in the world. I know who you are. I know who she is. And I want to help you take Maxx down."

She nods at a purple speedboat bobbing alongside. "I'll film from the Clickbait, of course," she adds, patting her helmet. "Heists are terrible for my hair."

Her camera, you notice, is already filming.
